messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated error rate on us-east-1 inference pool. 5xx spike, latency > 5s for multiple routes. autoscale attempted.
Maya Patel: saw the spike at 12:13 UTC, looks like continuous-batcher accumulated queue growth on batcher-42/43. GPU memory creeping then OOMs.
Ryan L: on it, pulling logs now. which customers hit?
Leo (Support): AcmeCorp and two smaller customers on dedicated pools reported timeouts and increased 504s. Customer-facing errors started ~12:10 UTC.
Jordan (SRE): nvidia-smi snapshot from node batcher-42:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
|  0  A100-SXM4-40GB   On        | 00000000:65:00.0 Off |                  0 |
| Processes:                                                            6 |
|   GPU Memory Usage: 38912 MiB / 40536 MiB                             |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Jordan (SRE): memory grows steadily then kernel crash: `E  : cudaMemcpyAsync failed: out of memory` repeated.
Carla G: batcher service logs show continuous-batcher accumulated 200k requests in accumulator before paging kicked in.
Maya Patel: looks like KV_PREFETCH + aggressive accumulation + long seq requests combo. prefix cache churn.
Ryan L: trying soft-mitigations: lowering batcher.accumulation_limit on the fly. patching config to cap at 32. applying to pool us-east-1/batchers via `rbctl apply` now.
oncall-bot: Deploy started by Ryan L — config/batcher/limit=32 to target:pool/us-east-1/batchers (deploy id d-20240312-01)
Maya Patel: also toggled telemetry to capture per-request sequence len and kvcache hits.
Jordan (SRE): observability: request size distribution shows a heavy tail — 2% of requests are 4x longer than usual, causing accumulation spike when they align.
Ryan L: applied limit, restarting batcher pods on 42/43 to drop their accumulators.
Carla G: restart logs show container restart due to SIGKILL after paging thrash. docker events: `containerd: oom` on pid 21234.
Leo (Support): patch note: told AcmeCorp we are investigating; asked them for any sudden workload changes. they replied they rolled a new prompt template at ~12:05.
Maya Patel: good catch — prompt change likely added long context. rolling back customer template request suggested.
Jordan (SRE): after restart, batcher memory stable-ish but still seeing intermittent `cudaLaunchKernel` errors on node 45.
Ryan L: node 45 has repeated PCI errors, driver logs: `NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus`. grabbing kernel dmesg.
Carla G: coordinating with infra: marking node45 for drain, creating cordon. `kubectl cordon node45 && kubectl drain node45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
oncall-bot: Node45 cordoned by Carla G (action id a-889)
Maya Patel: in parallel, disabling KV_PREFETCH on pool config to reduce prefetch memory pressure. `rbctl patch pool us-east-1 --set feature.kv_prefetch=false`
Jordan (SRE): aftermath: error rate down from 8% -> 1.5% after drains + config changes, p95 latency still elevated (1.2s -> 2.6s).
Ryan L: short term mitigation: increase reserved capacity by spinning up 4 extra batcher replicas with smaller accumulation_size so throughput persists but each replica uses less memory. issuing `rbctl scale pool/us-east-1 batchers +4 --override-accumulation=16`.
Leo (Support): AcmeCorp confirms immediate improvement in timeouts but some retries still failing. asked for ETA.
Maya Patel: ETA: continue 30m monitoring while infra drains remaining nodes. if stable, we'll leave kv_prefetch disabled and accumulation_limit reduced.
Jordan (SRE): discovered a bug: accumulator didn't decrement correctly when requests were timeout-cancelled, leaving stale slots and causing apparent growth. opened PR to fix (runtime/continuous-batcher#3245).
Carla G: can we hotfix?
Ryan L: we can backport a short patch that forces periodic accumulator compaction every 5s. preparing cherry-pick.
Maya Patel: rolling hotfix to batcher binary v1.12.3-fix-accum-compact to canary subset (batcher-46).
oncall-bot: Canary deploy started by Maya Patel — d-20240312-02 target batcher-46
Jordan (SRE): canary looks stable, memory not creeping for 12m.
Carla G: telemetry shows reduced stale accumulators count after canary.
Leo (Support): telling AcmeCorp we expect full remediation in ~45m; they appreciate the quick rollbacks.
Ryan L: also noticed some nodes had older CUDA driver (470.x) while others on 515.x — variance led to `cudaLaunchKernel` differences under memory pressure. raising infra ticket to standardize driver across pool.
Maya Patel: summary for next handoff:
- cause: combination of long-tail request contexts from customer prompt change + KV_PREFETCH + accumulator bug (didn't clear on cancellations) + driver heterogeneity.
- mitigations applied: cordon/drain node45, reduce accumulation_limit to 32 then 16 per replica, disabled KV_PREFETCH, scaled up smaller replicas, hotfix deployed (accum compact).
- customer impact: AcmeCorp + two smaller customers saw 504/timeout spike from ~12:10–12:25 UTC. partial recovery at 12:30 after restarts; p95 still slightly elevated until hotfix.
- outstanding: standardize CUDA drivers across pool, merge and roll out accumulator bug fix to stable channel, consider permanent default lowering of accumulation_limit and make kv_prefetch opt-in for long-context customers.
Jordan (SRE): logs/artifacts: attach crash dumps to ticket INF-9876, plus nvidia dmesg snippets and node audit logs.
Carla G: created incident postmortem draft under /incidents/INF-9876 for review. tagging engineering leads.
oncall-bot: Next oncall: Ryan L on duty until 16:00 UTC. Please acknowledge handoff.
Ryan L: acknowledged, will monitor dashboard for next 60m and follow up on driver ticket.
Maya Patel: thanks team, thanks Leo for CS updates. I'll keep KV_PREFETCH off for now and follow up on canary rollout.
Leo (Support): passing final note to AcmeCorp: they were offered a one-off throttle bypass while we tune defaults. they declined.
Jordan (SRE): minor follow-up: add e2e test that simulates long-tail prompt combinations against continuous-batcher to catch accumulator growth regressions.
Carla G: agreed; adding to eng-runtime sprint.
Ryan L: handoff complete. keeping this thread open for updates.
